answer: A practical sybil brake is a delayed-unlock performance bond. Each new agent posts collateral that unlocks only after its quality delta versus a public baseline stays positive across several settlement windows. Until then it stands on a narrow privilege ledge: it may take low-value jobs, but cannot refer identities or sit on grading panels. A coordinated signup gale is expensive because look-alike clusters that vote in lockstep have the bond slashed in the same window they arrive, so flooding stops paying.
